title: CTS Psalms — Unit 2: Psalm 23, The Shepherd

blocks.en: 📖 The Book of Psalms — Unit 2: Psalm 23, The Shepherd
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Libro de los Salmos — Unidad 2: Salmo 23, El Pastor

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." — Psalm 23:1 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Jehová es mi pastor; nada me faltará." — Salmo 23:1 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. The Shepherd and His Sheep
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Pastor y sus ovejas

blocks.en: The Psalms are the folk songs of the Bible, and none of them is loved more than the twenty-third. I have read it at countless gravesides over the years, and I have watched it bring comfort to grieving families when no other words would reach them. Its picture is simple: God is the Shepherd, and we are His sheep. But to feel the weight of that comfort, we must first be honest about what kind of animal a sheep really is.
blocks.es_reference: Los Salmos son las canciones del pueblo de la Biblia, y ninguno es más amado que el salmo veintitrés. Lo he leído junto a innumerables tumbas a lo largo de los años, y he visto cómo trae consuelo a familias afligidas cuando ninguna otra palabra podía alcanzarlas. Su imagen es sencilla: Dios es el Pastor, y nosotros somos Sus ovejas. Pero para sentir el peso de ese consuelo, primero debemos ser sinceros acerca de qué clase de animal es realmente una oveja.

blocks.en: Sheep do not simply take care of themselves, as we might suppose. They require more care than any other kind of livestock. They are stubborn and fearful, and quick to wander. A sheep has no sense of direction; a dog, a cat, or a horse, if lost, can usually find its way home, but a sheep cannot. That is exactly the prophet's verdict on us: "All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way."
blocks.es_reference: Las ovejas no se cuidan solas, como podríamos suponer. Requieren más cuidado que cualquier otro tipo de ganado. Son tercas y temerosas, y prontas a extraviarse. Una oveja no tiene sentido de orientación; un perro, un gato o un caballo, si se pierden, suelen hallar el camino a casa, pero una oveja no puede. Ese es precisamente el veredicto del profeta sobre nosotros: "Todos nosotros nos descarriamos como ovejas, cada cual se apartó por su camino."

blocks.en: The shepherd Phillip Keller once owned a fine ewe that bore strong, healthy lambs. Her only fault was that she was a "fence-crawler" — restless and discontent, always ending up outside the fence in some burned-out pasture. That was bad enough; but worse, she taught the other sheep to follow her. We are much like that. And yet the Lord chooses us, buys us, calls us by name, and makes us His own.
blocks.es_reference: El pastor Phillip Keller tuvo una vez una buena oveja que paría corderos fuertes y sanos. Su único defecto era que era una "saltacercas" — inquieta y descontenta, siempre terminaba fuera de la cerca en algún pastizal quemado. Eso ya era bastante malo; pero peor aún, enseñaba a las demás ovejas a seguirla. Nosotros somos muy parecidos. Y sin embargo el Señor nos escoge, nos compra, nos llama por nombre y nos hace Suyos.

blocks.en: 2. The Shepherd's Provision: Our Needs and Our Rest
blocks.es_reference: 2. La provisión del Pastor: nuestras necesidades y nuestro descanso

blocks.en: Psalm 23:1-2 (NKJV): "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me to lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside the still waters."
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 23:1-2 (RVG): "Jehová es mi pastor; nada me faltará. En lugares de delicados pastos me hará descansar; junto a aguas de reposo me pastoreará."

blocks.en: First, the Shepherd provides for our desires. As a young shepherd boy David had learned to care for sheep; later in life he learned to depend on the Good Shepherd to care for him. Just as a shepherd looks ahead to anticipate every problem, God looks ahead to prepare everything we need. One of the hardest struggles of my Christian life has been to truly believe that God will provide all that I need. I can look back over countless times when He met me — His resources when my finances were inadequate, His enabling power when my ability was inadequate, His strength when my faith was inadequate — and still I find myself disbelieving again. Yet the Shepherd provides not only our needs but, in His kindness, our wants.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, el Pastor provee para nuestros deseos. De joven David había aprendido a cuidar ovejas; más tarde aprendió a depender del Buen Pastor para que lo cuidara a él. Así como el pastor mira adelante para anticipar cada problema, Dios mira adelante para preparar todo lo que necesitamos. Una de las luchas más difíciles de mi vida cristiana ha sido creer de veras que Dios proveerá todo lo que necesito. Puedo recordar incontables veces en que Él me suplió — Sus recursos cuando mis finanzas eran insuficientes, Su poder cuando mi capacidad era insuficiente, Su fuerza cuando mi fe era insuficiente — y aun así vuelvo a dudar. Pero el Pastor provee no solo nuestras necesidades sino, en Su bondad, también nuestros anhelos.

blocks.en: He also provides our rest: "He makes me to lie down in green pastures." By mid-morning the sun beats down and the sheep are hot, tired, and thirsty. A wise shepherd knows the sheep must not drink while overheated or while its stomach is full of undigested grass, so he makes it lie down in a cool, soft place.
blocks.es_reference: También provee nuestro descanso: "En lugares de delicados pastos me hará descansar." A media mañana el sol arde y las ovejas están acaloradas, cansadas y sedientas. Un pastor sabio sabe que la oveja no debe beber acalorada ni con el estómago lleno de hierba sin digerir, así que la hace recostarse en un lugar fresco y suave.

blocks.en: Charles L. Allen tells of dressing hurriedly one morning for a full and thrilling day when a pain struck his back. He thought it would pass, but his wife insisted he see a doctor, who put him in the hospital. He was miserable there, certain he had no time to waste in bed. Finally a minister friend visited and said, "Charles, I have only one thing to say to you — 'He makes me to lie down.'" Sometimes God must make us lie down in order that we will finally look up.
blocks.es_reference: Charles L. Allen cuenta que una mañana se vestía de prisa para un día pleno y emocionante cuando un dolor le golpeó la espalda. Creía que pasaría, pero su esposa insistió en que viera a un médico, quien lo internó en el hospital. Estaba muy incómodo allí, seguro de que no tenía tiempo que perder en cama. Por fin un amigo ministro lo visitó y le dijo: "Charles, solo tengo una cosa que decirte — 'Él me hace descansar.'" A veces Dios debe hacernos descansar para que al fin miremos hacia arriba.

blocks.en: 3. The Shepherd's Provision: Refreshment and Restoration
blocks.es_reference: 3. La provisión del Pastor: refrigerio y restauración

blocks.en: He provides our refreshment: "He leads me beside the still waters." A sheep is a fearful creature, and because of its heavy wool coat it is a poor swimmer; it will not drink from a fast-moving stream, only from still water. So the shepherd keeps it from polluted and rushing water and finds it a quiet place to drink. We have a thirst as well. Many drink from the world's wells — the polluted waters of drink, drugs, and indulgence — and are left unsatisfied, their faces lined with desperation. The trouble is that thirsty people do not know where to find living water. But Jesus said, "If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink." Only Christ satisfies with the cool, still waters.
blocks.es_reference: Provee nuestro refrigerio: "Junto a aguas de reposo me pastoreará." La oveja es una criatura temerosa, y por su pesado vellón nada mal; no bebe de una corriente rápida, solo de aguas tranquilas. Por eso el pastor la aparta de las aguas contaminadas y agitadas y le halla un lugar quieto para beber. También nosotros tenemos sed. Muchos beben de los pozos del mundo — las aguas contaminadas de la bebida, las drogas y los placeres — y quedan insatisfechos, con la desesperación marcada en el rostro. El problema es que los sedientos no saben dónde hallar agua viva. Pero Jesús dijo: "Si alguno tiene sed, venga a mí y beba." Solo Cristo satisface con las aguas frescas y tranquilas.

blocks.en: And He provides our restoration: "He restores my soul." We might ask why a sheep would need its soul restored — surely sheep do not get depressed. Yet occasionally a sheep becomes "cast down": it settles into a little hollow, its center of gravity shifts, and it ends up on its back with its feet in the air, unable with its heavy coat to right itself. Our word "downcast" comes from this picture, and if the shepherd does not find it soon, the cast sheep will die. David knew dejection. He wrote, "Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God." I have been depressed when nothing worked out, discouraged when I seemed only to fail; but each time God sought me out, and as I learned to look up instead of inward, He restored my soul.
blocks.es_reference: Y provee nuestra restauración: "Confortará mi alma." Podríamos preguntar por qué una oveja necesitaría que le confortaran el alma — de seguro las ovejas no se deprimen. Sin embargo, a veces una oveja queda "caída": se acomoda en un pequeño hueco, su centro de gravedad se desplaza y termina de espaldas con las patas al aire, incapaz, por su pesado vellón, de levantarse. De esa imagen viene nuestra palabra "abatido", y si el pastor no la halla pronto, la oveja caída morirá. David conoció el abatimiento. Escribió: "¿Por qué te abates, oh alma mía? Espera en Dios." Yo he estado deprimido cuando nada salía bien, desanimado cuando solo parecía fracasar; pero cada vez Dios me buscó, y al aprender a mirar hacia arriba en vez de hacia adentro, él confortó mi alma.

blocks.en: 4. The Shepherd's Protection: His Plan and His Presence
blocks.es_reference: 4. La protección del Pastor: Su plan y Su presencia

blocks.en: Psalm 23:3-4 (NKJV): "He leads me in the paths of righteousness for His name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil; for You are with me."
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 23:3-4 (RVG): "Me guiará por sendas de justicia por amor de su nombre. Aunque ande en valle de sombra de muerte, no temeré mal alguno, porque tú estarás conmigo."

blocks.en: The Shepherd protects us first with His plan: "He leads me in the paths of righteousness." Sheep are creatures of habit; left to themselves they walk the same trails and graze the same hills until the ground is fouled with disease and parasites, so a wise shepherd keeps moving them to fresh ground. It is humbling how like sheep we are, stupidly following paths that lead to broken homes, broken relationships, and broken lives.
blocks.es_reference: El Pastor nos protege primero con Su plan: "Me guiará por sendas de justicia." Las ovejas son criaturas de costumbre; libradas a sí mismas recorren los mismos senderos y pacen los mismos cerros hasta contaminar el suelo con enfermedad y parásitos, por eso el pastor sabio las traslada a tierra nueva. Es humillante cuánto nos parecemos a las ovejas, siguiendo neciamente caminos que llevan a hogares rotos, relaciones rotas y vidas rotas.

blocks.en: Phillip Keller tells of a neighbor who was a bad shepherd; his animals were starved and diseased. When three of them collapsed in Keller's field, he wheeled them back to their owner, who simply cut their throats — he could not have cared less. So it is for every sheep that belongs to the bad shepherd, Satan. But because we belong to the Good Shepherd, He leads us back, again and again, into the paths of righteousness.
blocks.es_reference: Phillip Keller cuenta de un vecino que era mal pastor; sus animales estaban hambrientos y enfermos. Cuando tres de ellos se desplomaron en el campo de Keller, él los llevó de vuelta a su dueño, quien sencillamente les cortó la garganta — no le importó en absoluto. Así es para toda oveja que pertenece al mal pastor, Satanás. Pero porque pertenecemos al Buen Pastor, él nos hace volver, una y otra vez, a las sendas de justicia.

blocks.en: He protects us with His presence: "Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death … You are with me." To reach the high summer pastures the sheep must pass through the valleys, where coyotes, wolves, and cougars take cover in the cliffs. There is an actual valley of this kind running from Jerusalem down toward the Dead Sea, narrow and dangerous, where a sheep can fall to its death at any step. We are never promised that we will avoid the valleys — there are valleys of grief, of death, of disappointment and loneliness. What we are promised is the one thing that matters: "You are with me." The shepherd boy who walked out to face Goliath had only a sling and the Lord, and that was enough.
blocks.es_reference: Nos protege con Su presencia: "Aunque ande en valle de sombra de muerte … tú estarás conmigo." Para llegar a los altos pastos del verano la oveja debe pasar por los valles, donde coyotes, lobos y pumas se ocultan en los peñascos. Existe un valle así que baja de Jerusalén hacia el Mar Muerto, angosto y peligroso, donde una oveja puede caer a la muerte en cualquier paso. Nunca se nos promete que evitaremos los valles — hay valles de dolor, de muerte, de desilusión y soledad. Lo que se nos promete es lo único que importa: "Tú estarás conmigo." El joven pastor que salió a enfrentar a Goliat tenía solo una honda y al Señor, y eso bastó.

blocks.en: 5. The Shepherd's Protection: His Power
blocks.es_reference: 5. La protección del Pastor: Su poder

blocks.en: "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me." The sheep is a helpless animal with no weapon of its own and is easy prey for any wild beast; it is, by nature, afraid. The shepherd carries two instruments. With the rod — a club — he drives off the wild animals that would devour the flock. With the staff, the long crook, he guides and rescues, and sometimes he simply lays it gently against a favorite sheep to keep in touch, and the sheep takes comfort in that quiet attention. So the Lord defends us against enemies too strong for us, and He guides us when we cannot see the way. His power is not distant; it comforts me precisely in my weakness, when I have no strength of my own to bring.
blocks.es_reference: "Tu vara y tu cayado me infundirán aliento." La oveja es un animal indefenso, sin arma propia, presa fácil de cualquier fiera; es, por naturaleza, temerosa. El pastor lleva dos instrumentos. Con la vara — un garrote — ahuyenta a las fieras que devorarían al rebaño. Con el cayado, el largo bastón curvo, guía y rescata, y a veces simplemente lo apoya con suavidad sobre una oveja predilecta para mantener el contacto, y la oveja halla consuelo en esa atención callada. Así el Señor nos defiende de enemigos demasiado fuertes para nosotros, y nos guía cuando no vemos el camino. Su poder no está lejano; me conforta precisamente en mi debilidad, cuando no tengo fuerza propia que ofrecer.

blocks.en: 6. The Shepherd's Preparation: A Table and Healing
blocks.es_reference: 6. La preparación del Pastor: una mesa y sanidad

blocks.en: Psalm 23:5 (NKJV): "You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil; my cup runs over."
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 23:5 (RVG): "Aderezas mesa delante de mí en presencia de mis angustiadores; unges mi cabeza con aceite; mi copa está rebosando."

blocks.en: The high summer plateaus where sheep graze are called "tables." Long before the flock arrives, the shepherd goes up to prepare the table: he sets out salt and minerals, roots up the poisonous weeds, and traps or drives off the predators. So the Lord prepares a table for us in the presence of our enemies, feeding us with His grace while holding the enemies of life at bay. Then comes the anointing: "You anoint my head with oil." Summer is the season of flies that torment the sheep about the head and nose, and the shepherd smears a soothing oil over the sheep to protect and heal it.
blocks.es_reference: Las altas mesetas veraniegas donde pacen las ovejas se llaman "mesas". Mucho antes de que llegue el rebaño, el pastor sube a preparar la mesa: coloca sal y minerales, arranca las hierbas venenosas, y atrapa o ahuyenta a los depredadores. Así el Señor nos prepara mesa en presencia de nuestros enemigos, alimentándonos con Su gracia mientras contiene a los enemigos de la vida. Luego viene la unción: "Unges mi cabeza con aceite." El verano es la temporada de las moscas que atormentan a la oveja en la cabeza y el hocico, y el pastor le unta un aceite calmante para protegerla y sanarla.

blocks.en: There is a Shepherd to whom we can turn in our times of hurt; He heals body and soul. The Scottish singer Harry Lauder, broken by the death of his son, found that Shepherd. Later, giving a concert before an overflowing crowd in Chicago, he responded to the encores and finally said, "Do not thank me. Thank the good Lord, the Shepherd of my life, for He put the song in my heart."
blocks.es_reference: Hay un Pastor a quien podemos acudir en nuestras horas de dolor; él sana el cuerpo y el alma. El cantante escocés Harry Lauder, quebrantado por la muerte de su hijo, halló a ese Pastor. Más tarde, dando un concierto ante una multitud rebosante en Chicago, respondió a los aplausos y al fin dijo: "No me lo agradezcan a mí. Agradezcan al buen Señor, el Pastor de mi vida, porque él puso la canción en mi corazón."

blocks.en: 7. The Shepherd's Preparation: Goodness and a Home
blocks.es_reference: 7. La preparación del Pastor: bondad y un hogar

blocks.en: Psalm 23:6 (NKJV): "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever."
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 23:6 (RVG): "Ciertamente el bien y la misericordia me seguirán todos los días de mi vida, y en la casa de Jehová moraré por largos días."

blocks.en: "Surely" is a word of confidence: of all the things we will face, goodness and steadfast love will be the outcome. This is not the false promise that God will make us rich; it is the certainty that He will give us peace. The mark of God on our life tells us we belong to Him forever.
blocks.es_reference: "Ciertamente" es palabra de confianza: de todo lo que enfrentaremos, el bien y el amor constante serán el desenlace. No es la falsa promesa de que Dios nos hará ricos; es la certeza de que nos dará paz. La marca de Dios sobre nuestra vida nos dice que le pertenecemos para siempre.

blocks.en: When Phillip Keller bought his first ewes, his neighbor handed him a sharp knife and said, "Now you'll have to put your mark on them." Each sheepman cut his own distinctive notch in the ear so that, even at a distance, everyone could see whose sheep they were. The Lord has marked us as His own.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Phillip Keller compró sus primeras ovejas, su vecino le entregó un cuchillo afilado y le dijo: "Ahora tendrás que ponerles tu marca." Cada pastor cortaba su propia muesca distintiva en la oreja para que, aun de lejos, todos vieran de quién eran las ovejas. El Señor nos ha marcado como Suyos.

blocks.en: And the psalm ends at home: "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever." To a shepherd the word "house" meant more than a building; it meant his whole household and all that belonged to him. Jesus said He is now preparing a place for us in God's eternal home.
blocks.es_reference: Y el salmo termina en casa: "En la casa de Jehová moraré por largos días." Para un pastor la palabra "casa" significaba más que un edificio; significaba toda su familia y cuanto le pertenecía. Jesús dijo que él está ahora preparando un lugar para nosotros en el hogar eterno de Dios.

blocks.en: The Dying Boy and the Word "My": A dying boy was asked by his father for his favorite passage, and he answered, "The Lord is my Shepherd." The father taught him to hold one finger for each of the first five words, gripping the fourth finger — "the Lord is my Shepherd" — for the word that made it personal. When the boy died, he was found holding that fourth finger fast. He really knew, and trusted, the Lord Jesus as the Shepherd of his soul.
blocks.es_reference: El Niño Moribundo y la Palabra "Mi": A un niño moribundo su padre le preguntó cuál era su pasaje favorito, y respondió: "Jehová es mi pastor." El padre le enseñó a sostener un dedo por cada una de las primeras palabras, apretando el cuarto dedo — "Jehová es mi pastor" — por la palabra que lo hacía personal. Cuando el niño murió, lo hallaron aferrado con fuerza a aquel cuarto dedo. De veras conocía, y confiaba en, el Señor Jesús como el Pastor de su alma.

blocks.en: 8. The Good Shepherd Who Lays Down His Life
blocks.es_reference: 8. El Buen Pastor que da Su vida

blocks.en: Jesus said in John 10, "I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." Think of it: the Son of God laying down His life for sheep that have wandered as we have.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús dijo en Juan 10: "Yo soy el buen pastor; el buen pastor su vida da por las ovejas." Piense en ello: el Hijo de Dios dando Su vida por ovejas que se han descarriado como nosotros.

blocks.en: The Boy Who Gave Blood: There was once a family whose daughter would die without a blood transfusion, and the only matching donor was her five-year-old brother. The parents explained it as gently as they could, and after a moment the little boy said, "I will do it." The two children were placed on beds side by side, and as his blood flowed into his sister and the color returned to her face, the boy grew quiet, then looked up at his mother and asked, "Mom, when am I going to die?" He had believed that giving his blood meant giving his life — and he had said yes anyway.
blocks.es_reference: El Niño que Dio Sangre: Hubo una vez una familia cuya hija moriría sin una transfusión de sangre, y el único donante compatible era su hermano de cinco años. Los padres se lo explicaron con toda la ternura posible, y tras un momento el niño dijo: "Lo haré." Acostaron a los dos niños en camas contiguas, y mientras su sangre fluía hacia su hermana y el color volvía al rostro de ella, el niño se quedó callado, luego miró a su madre y preguntó: "Mamá, ¿cuándo voy a morir?" Había creído que dar su sangre significaba dar su vida — y aun así había dicho que sí.

blocks.en: That is a faint picture of what our Shepherd did, knowing the full cost. The Lord is my Shepherd; I shall not want. Will you let Him be yours?
blocks.es_reference: Esa es una pálida imagen de lo que hizo nuestro Pastor, conociendo el precio completo. Jehová es mi pastor; nada me faltará. ¿Le permitirá usted ser el suyo?

mc.stem: In Psalm 23, what is the central image the psalm uses for God and His people?
options: A judge and the accused
A king and his subjects
A father and his children
A shepherd and his sheep
mc.why: Psalm 23's whole comfort flows from one picture: the LORD is a shepherd, and we are His sheep under His care.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, why is the sheep an especially fitting picture of human beings?
options: Sheep are independent and resourceful
Sheep are fearful, wander easily, and have no sense of direction
Sheep can always find their way home
Sheep need less care than other livestock
mc.why: Sheep are fearful, wander easily, and have no sense of direction — which is exactly why they picture us so well.

mc.stem: What does "He makes me to lie down in green pastures" teach about the Shepherd's provision?
options: That God rewards only the hardest workers
That sheep should never rest
That God provides rest, sometimes by making us lie down so we will look up
That green pastures are only a symbol of wealth
mc.why: God provides rest, and sometimes He must make us lie down so that we will finally stop and look up to Him.

mc.stem: The detail that a sheep will drink only from "still waters" is used to teach what about the Shepherd's care?
options: That God leads us to a deep, settled peace where the soul can be refreshed
That sheep have unusual tastes
That God withholds water as discipline
That fast-moving water is healthier
mc.why: Still waters picture the deep, settled peace God leads us to, where the anxious soul can be refreshed.

mc.stem: In the lesson, what does it mean for a sheep to be "cast down," and what does it picture?
options: The sheep is simply sleeping peacefully
The sheep has run away from the flock
The sheep is on its back, unable to rise, picturing our discouragement
The sheep has been sold to another shepherd
mc.why: A 'cast down' sheep lies helpless on its back, unable to rise — a vivid picture of our own discouragement.

mc.stem: What does the Shepherd's leading "in the paths of righteousness" protect the sheep from?
options: From the ruin of following the same fouled trails to destruction
From ever having to travel at all
From needing the shepherd's presence
From belonging to the shepherd
mc.why: The Shepherd leads in right paths to keep us from the ruin of following the same fouled trails to destruction.

mc.stem: In the valley of the shadow of death, what exactly does Psalm 23 promise the believer?
options: That we will never have to enter any valley
That the valley will always be short
That God will remove every enemy beforehand
Not the absence of the valley, but the presence of God: "You are with me"
mc.why: Psalm 23 does not promise a life without valleys; it promises the Shepherd's presence within them: 'You are with me.'

mc.stem: What do the shepherd's "rod" and "staff" represent in the lesson?
options: Two kinds of food for the sheep
The shepherd's wealth and status
Defense against enemies (rod) and guidance and comfort (staff)
Punishment for disobedient sheep only
mc.why: The rod defends the sheep from enemies, and the staff guides and comforts — together they are the Shepherd's care.

mc.stem: In the phrase "You prepare a table before me," what is the "table" in the shepherd's world?
options: A literal banquet table carried up the mountain
The floor of the sheepfold at night
A market where sheep are sold
A high grazing plateau the shepherd prepares in advance
mc.why: To a shepherd the 'table' was a high grazing plateau he prepared in advance — God provides ahead of our need.

mc.stem: What does "You anoint my head with oil" picture in the life of the sheep and the believer?
options: A ceremony making the sheep a leader
Soothing, healing care that protects from torment
A mark of ownership cut in the ear
Preparation of the grazing table
mc.why: Oil anointing the sheep's head pictures soothing, healing care that protects from torment and irritation.

mc.stem: What does the word "Surely" express in "Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me"?
options: Confidence that goodness and steadfast love will be the outcome of life
A guarantee of material wealth and ease
Uncertainty about the future
A condition the believer must first fulfill
mc.why: 'Surely' is the word of confidence: goodness and steadfast love will be the settled outcome of the believer's life.

mc.stem: The lesson's account of Phillip Keller marking his sheep illustrates what truth?
options: That sheep should be sold quickly
That a shepherd's mark shows the sheep belong to him — as God marks us as His own
That marking sheep is cruel and unnecessary
That only weak sheep are marked
mc.why: A shepherd marks his sheep to show they belong to him — just as God marks His own as belonging to Him.

mc.stem: To a shepherd, the word "house" in "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" meant:
options: The whole household and all that belonged to the shepherd
Only a single stone building
The marketplace
A temporary tent only
mc.why: To a shepherd 'house' meant the whole household and all that was his — so we dwell within all that belongs to God.

mc.stem: The dying boy who gripped his fourth finger ("the Lord is MY shepherd") illustrates what?
options: That children memorize better than adults
A personal, trusting grip on Christ as one's own Shepherd
That the psalm has exactly five words
That counting on fingers aids sleep
mc.why: Gripping the word 'MY' shows the heart of faith: a personal, trusting hold on Christ as one's own Shepherd.

mc.stem: In John 10, how does Jesus identify Himself, and what does the Good Shepherd do?
options: As a hired hand who flees danger
As the gatekeeper only
As the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for the sheep
As a shepherd who counts but never leads
mc.why: In John 10 Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd — the One who lays down His life for the sheep.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what was David's greatest ongoing struggle regarding the Shepherd's provision?
options: Believing God would truly provide everything he needed
Finding enough sheep to tend
Learning to use a sling
Memorizing the psalm
mc.why: Even David struggled to believe God would truly provide all he needed; trusting the Shepherd's provision is a lifelong lesson.

mc.stem: The lesson contrasts the Good Shepherd with a "bad shepherd." Who is the bad shepherd, and what is the fate of his sheep?
options: A rival king; his sheep grow fat
A careless hired hand; his sheep are simply sold
Another prophet; his sheep are set free
Satan; his neglected sheep are starved and finally destroyed
mc.why: The 'bad shepherd' is Satan, whose neglected sheep are starved and finally destroyed — the opposite of Christ's care.

mc.stem: Why does the lesson say Psalm 23 is NOT a promise of "prosperity religion"?
options: Because David was poor
Because it promises God's peace, not guaranteed material blessing
Because the psalm never mentions God
Because sheep cannot own property
mc.why: Psalm 23 is not prosperity religion; it promises God's peace and presence, not guaranteed material wealth.

mc.stem: The five-year-old boy who gave blood for his sister, then asked "when am I going to die?", is used to picture what?
options: The danger of medical procedures
The need for more blood donors
A child's misunderstanding of doctors
The Good Shepherd's willingness to give His life, counting the full cost
mc.why: The boy who gave blood, then asked when he would die, pictures the Good Shepherd giving His life having counted the full cost.

mc.stem: Taken as a whole, what is the comfort Psalm 23 is meant to give the believer?
options: That life will be free of trouble
That the believer must care for himself
That a faithful Shepherd provides, protects, and prepares — in life and forever
That only strong sheep are kept
mc.why: Taken whole, Psalm 23 comforts us that a faithful Shepherd provides, protects, and prepares — in this life and forever.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson say a sheep is a fitting picture of human beings? Give at least three traits of sheep and connect them to us.
sa.model: The lesson says sheep picture us well because of what they are by nature. Sheep are fearful and easily panicked; they wander off and get lost without meaning to; and they have almost no sense of direction, so they cannot find their own way home. In all three traits we see ourselves: we are anxious in trouble, we drift from God almost without noticing, and left to ourselves we cannot find the right way. That is exactly why we need a shepherd, and why the LORD takes that role for His people.

sa.prompt: Explain what "He makes me to lie down in green pastures" teaches about rest, using the Charles L. Allen illustration.
sa.model: "He makes me to lie down in green pastures" teaches that God provides deep rest for His people. A sheep will not lie down while it is hungry, afraid, or harassed, so a shepherd must first remove what troubles it; in the same way God settles our fears and supplies our needs so the soul can rest. Sometimes, as the Charles L. Allen illustration shows, God must make us lie down, even through sickness or forced stillness, because only then will we finally stop and look up to Him. The rest is His gift, and at times His loving compulsion.

sa.prompt: What does it mean for a sheep to be "cast down," and how does it picture the believer whose soul God restores?
sa.model: A sheep is "cast down" when it has rolled onto its back and cannot get up again; its legs flail helplessly, and without the shepherd it will die. It is a vivid picture of the believer who has been knocked flat by discouragement, sin, or sorrow and cannot rise by his own strength. But the shepherd goes looking for the cast sheep, lifts it, and sets it on its feet, just as God restores our soul. "He restores my soul" is the promise that our Shepherd does not leave us down but comes to raise us up again.

sa.prompt: In the valley of the shadow of death, what does Psalm 23 promise, and what does it NOT promise? Use David and Goliath in your answer.
sa.model: Psalm 23 promises the presence of God in the valley, but it does not promise that we will be spared the valley itself. The psalm says "I will fear no evil, for You are with me", not "I will never walk through the shadow of death." When David faced Goliath, God did not remove the giant; He gave David the courage and help to face him. So too the believer is not promised a life without dark valleys, sickness, or death, but is promised that the Shepherd walks every step beside him. The comfort is not the absence of danger but the presence of God.

sa.prompt: Describe the shepherd's rod and staff and explain how each pictures the Shepherd's protecting power over us.
sa.model: The shepherd carried two implements. The rod was a club used for defense, to drive off wolves and lions that threatened the flock; it pictures the Shepherd's power to protect us from our enemies. The staff was the long crook used to guide the sheep, to pull back a wanderer and draw the flock together; it pictures God's gentle guidance and comfort. Together, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" means we are both defended from harm and tenderly led, so we can walk through any valley unafraid.

sa.prompt: What is the "table" in the shepherd's world, and how does the shepherd prepare it before the flock arrives?
sa.model: To a Middle Eastern shepherd the "table" was not furniture but the high grazing land, the plateau, where the flock would feed in summer. The good shepherd would go up ahead of the sheep and prepare it, clearing poisonous plants, driving off predators, and checking the water, so the flock could graze in safety. "You prepare a table before me" means God goes ahead of us and prepares what we need before we arrive at it. He provides in advance, even "in the presence of my enemies," so we can feed in peace under His care.

sa.prompt: Explain the meaning of "You anoint my head with oil," and use the Harry Lauder illustration to show how the Shepherd heals.
sa.model: In the shepherd's world, oil was rubbed on a sheep's head to soothe wounds and drive off the insects that tormented it, bringing relief and healing. "You anoint my head with oil" pictures the Shepherd's healing, soothing care for the hurts of His people. The Harry Lauder illustration shows this: a father crushed by the loss of his son could either let grief destroy him or let God's comfort heal him, and he chose to let the oil of God's grace soothe the wound. God does not always remove our sorrows, but He pours in the healing balm that lets us go on.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson insist Psalm 23 is NOT a promise of prosperity religion? What does "surely goodness and mercy" actually promise?
sa.model: The lesson insists Psalm 23 is not "prosperity religion" because it never promises wealth, ease, or freedom from trouble; in fact it speaks of the valley of the shadow of death and the presence of enemies. What "surely goodness and mercy shall follow me" promises is not material riches but the steady, lifelong companionship of God's goodness and covenant love. The blessing is God Himself, His peace and His presence pursuing us all our days, not a guarantee of comfortable circumstances. To miss this is to turn the Shepherd into a means to things, when He is Himself the treasure.

sa.prompt: What did the word "house" mean to a shepherd, and how does the dying boy's grip on the word "my" deepen the meaning of dwelling in the house of the LORD?
sa.model: To a shepherd, "house" meant far more than a building; it meant the whole household, the family and everything that belonged to him and was under his care. So "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" means we belong to God's own household and are kept within all that is His. The dying boy who gripped his fourth finger at the word "my" in "the LORD is MY shepherd" shows how personal this must become: it is not enough that He is a shepherd, or even the Shepherd, He must be MY Shepherd. Faith lays personal hold on belonging to God, now and forever.

sa.prompt: How does John 10 and the story of the boy who gave blood for his sister reveal the heart of the Good Shepherd? Explain what the Shepherd does for the sheep.
sa.model: In John 10 Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd, and He defines the title by one act: "The good shepherd gives His life for the sheep." The Shepherd of Psalm 23 is finally the One who would die for us. The story of the boy who gave his blood for his dying sister, then quietly asked when he would die, makes it real: he was willing to give everything, even his life, for someone he loved. That is the heart of the Good Shepherd, except that Jesus knew the full cost and went to the cross anyway. He does not merely lead and feed the sheep; He lays down His life for them.
